subject: Meteorology
title: Microbursts
description: A micro-lesson that makes Microbursts usable.

hook.text: A microburst is a sudden, powerful downdraft that hits the ground and spreads out—a lethal threat during landing.

buildup.text: Aircraft entering a microburst first encounter a headwind (extra lift), then a downdraft, then a tailwind (lost lift).

discovery.text: The transition from headwind to tailwind can cause sudden airspeed loss of 80+ knots—enough to crash an airliner.

twist.text: Dry microbursts produce no rain—they're invisible yet just as dangerous as wet ones with visible precipitation.

climax.text: After multiple fatal crashes, airports installed LLWAS and TDWR systems—microburst alerts are now routine.

punchline.text: A column of crashing air—invisible, sudden, and once deadly.

quiz.question: What makes microbursts especially dangerous during landing?
options: Rapid airspeed loss from headwind-to-tailwind shift
